name: TX-29
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +17 partisan lean
Incumbent Sylvia Garcia running for reelection with a large fundraising edge
Republican challenger Martha Fierro has raised no money
Prediction markets price Garcia at about 97% to win
model.rationale: Garcia holds a Houston-area seat with a +17 Democratic lean, has out-raised her opponent by roughly $1 million to zero, and benefits from outside spending while facing none. With no polls or expert ratings available, the fundamentals and market pricing both point to an easy incumbent win.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or unexpected outside spending against Garcia would be the first sign of trouble.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Sylvia Garcia seeks another term in a Houston-area district that leans Democratic by about 17 points. She enters the general election with a renomination secured, nearly $1 million raised, and more than $560,000 in outside support, while Republican Martha Fierro has reported no fundraising and no outside help.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price Garcia near 97%. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and a lopsided money advantage makes this a Safe Democratic seat, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty about the exact margin.
